North America.name: Austin, Texas
North America.message: 2023 COTA F1 race! The city itself was okay, probably as good as it gets in Texas. Cool street art.

North America.name: Bellingham, Washington
North America.message: I thought this would be my future home for a while, until I realized how much I like larger cities. Still a great retreat location! Makeworth Coffee Roasters is the place to go. Edit: this was unexpectedly my home for the summer of 2025!

North America.name: Bozeman, Montana
North America.message: Apparently it was opening week at the college. Every hotel fully booked, so slept in the Rav4 with Aurora.

North America.name: Brule, Wisconsin
North America.message: This is where I grew up. It's a town of 600 people, a gas station, diner, and four bars. I somehow made it out of here!

North America.name: Chicago, Illinois
North America.message: For how close this is to home, I should have gone here more often. Only once so far. I can see the appeal of living here, but deep-dish pizza sucks and I cannot assimilate.

North America.name: Coeur d'Alene, Idaho
North America.message: I forgot my doggy poop bags in the car. I'm so so sorry please forgive me it won't happen again (great city btw)

North America.name: Columbia, South Carolina
North America.message: The home of my obsession for libraries. I've found several I like more since visiting in 2023, but the Richland Library will always be special to me!

North America.name: Copper Harbor, Michigan
North America.message: Copper Harbor is where it's at. There's lots of great trails to explore, best done when the leaves are changing colors!

North America.name: Duluth, Minnesota
North America.message: Got my degree here. Went back here after my trip around the world. Will probably be back here again. Go Bulldogs!

North America.name: Eau Claire, Wisconsin
North America.message: My first true love. Eau Claire is such a beautiful city - just a shame it's in Wisconsin. Lots of great biking around here.

North America.name: Fergus Falls, Minnesota
North America.message: A place I called home during the entirety of COVID. I miss my house and the friends I made, but not so much the city itself.

North America.name: Grand Canyon National Park
North America.message: Have been to the Grand Canyon twice and loved it both times. Need to go back some day and complete rim-rim-rim.

North America.name: Indianapolis, Indiana
North America.message: Union 50 served me the best meal I've had in my life.

North America.name: Lake Forest Park, Washington
North America.message: This was actually my first home in Seattle, but it's easier to just say Seattle.

North America.name: Miami, Florida
North America.message: Did a 5k run by myself during a tropical storm.

North America.name: Minneapolis, Minnesota
North America.message: A place I called home for a few years, but never really experienced.

North America.name: Navarre, Florida
North America.message: How on earth did I end up living here?!? Just a short three month stay in a camper near the beach.

North America.name: New York, New York
North America.message: Maybe a bit too big for Big City Nick. Still a nice city to explore.

North America.name: Olympic National Park
North America.message: Cemented my love for the PNW.

North America.name: Palm Beach, Florida
North America.message: Spent $400 total for a 4-night vacation.

North America.name: Rugby, North Dakota
North America.message: They say Rugby is the geographical center of North America. It's not, but they say it is.

North America.name: Seattle, Washington
North America.message: It took 11 years, but Seattle is finally the place I call home! So excited to see what happens next.

North America.name: Washington, D.C.
North America.message: Visited three times in 13 months - and not at all prior to or since. Much more to do and see here.

Europe.name: Amsterdam, Netherlands
Europe.message: It's Amsterdam. What more needs to be said?! (P.S. - the red light district is in the center of the city, so if you always get a hotel in the center of the city, be aware of that.)

Europe.name: Antwerp, Belgium
Europe.message: Spent a few nights. Ate some chocolate. One of the most incredible train stations I've come across.

Europe.name: Basel, Switzerland
Europe.message: The hostel in Prague messed up my extension, so I left and took an overnight train to Zürich. In my spontaneity I then decided to get off at 7AM in Basel instead. One of my favs!

Europe.name: Belgrade, Serbia
Europe.message: The people are nice, but avoid pork at all costs. I'll be back when they fix their air quality.

Europe.name: Berlin, Germany
Europe.message: Loved the city. Met some great people. Anna taught me how intercity trains work, Kasia showed me how to use the S-Bahn, Stranger Chess learned me how to lose at chess.

Europe.name: Bolzano, Italy
Europe.message: Quintessential Italy. Would have been content leaving for another country after spending the afternoon here.

Europe.name: Borås, Sweden
Europe.message: There was a train derailment between here and Gothenburg so I was forced to get off and take a bus. I decided to walk around and have dinner. Why not!

Europe.name: Bruges, Belgium
Europe.message: Bruges is unique, but not my kind of unique. If you like history, this is the place for you.

Europe.name: Brussels, Belgium
Europe.message: People told me Brussels is boring, but I kind of liked exploring. Went back in 2026 and the St Michael & St Gudula Cathedral has some of the most impressive stained glass I've ever seen (and is free)!

Europe.name: Budapest, Hungary
Europe.message: Home of Ernő Rubik, and cube stores selling at 5x MSRP. Actually beautiful though. A city I recommend to most. The central market is one of the best I saw anywhere.

Europe.name: Cologne, Germany
Europe.message: The cathedral wouldn't let me in with my pre-purchased ticket, so I walked around until I found a pride parade. I'll let you guess who was more welcoming.

Europe.name: Copenhagen, Denmark
Europe.message: Very Hygge. Still don't know what that means, but you'll find it here. Hostel group was top notch. Went to a flea market under an overpass and a day in Malmö with Delissa (Melissa with a D, as she reminded me the fifth time I forgot).

Europe.name: Dresden, Germany
Europe.message: An afternoon stop on the way to Prague. The creamery was very unique. I do not recommend the buttermilk.

Europe.name: Florence, Italy
Europe.message: They replaced all the parks with paintings. I'm not sure I like that trade. Still lots of culture to see and explore.

Europe.name: Gdańsk, Poland
Europe.message: Home of the world renowned Żuraw M3 crane. Climbed for a view over the shipyards. Quiet canals and narrow alleys otherwise.

Europe.name: Ghent, Belgium
Europe.message: Ghent. Ghent... I went to Ghent? Oh yeah! Super cool library. And first time using a train-station locker like I'm some kind of hero (or villain??) in a Bourne movie.

Europe.name: Gothenburg, Sweden
Europe.message: It was just another nice city, as you'd expect in Sweden. Went to the Supergirl movie in theaters because it was hot out. Unfortunately, the subtitles being in Swedish was more of an issue than I expected, given all the alien dialogue.

Europe.name: Graz, Austria
Europe.message: Slept in a hostel next to the train station. Climbed the clocktower hill in the morning, got a coffee, left.

Europe.name: Helsinki, Finland
Europe.message: A calm and friendly city which I frequent. Considered immigrating to Finland to move here, and spent a month living in Kamppi.

Europe.name: Innsbruck, Austria
Europe.message: Cable car to the top and a hike the last few feet to the peak for the first snow of the trip, despite Finland having been below freezing in September. Also where I met the Taiwanese woman who told me Raohe night market was the one thing I had to do in Taipei.

Europe.name: Kalajoki, Finland
Europe.message: Kalajoki is the home of my grandmother - a short trip to visit her gravestone and the land she grew up on. Edit: 2025 return, now inherited the land with my siblings. Future cabin??

Europe.name: Katowice, Poland
Europe.message: One of my favorite places in Europe. Light rain on the ground, neon reflecting off everything, trams appearing from three directions at once. A city from the future, in the past.

Europe.name: Kaunas, Lithuania
Europe.message: A few good hours on the way to Warsaw. Find the Kiemo Galerija - a small outdoor "yard gallery" tucked into a courtyard.

Europe.name: Košice, Slovakia
Europe.message: Discovered the blue-wrapper Slovak KitKat alternative here, which I did not appreciate until I'd left the country and couldn't get any more.

Europe.name: Kraków, Poland
Europe.message: My actual goal here was to find an internet café and play Counter-Strike for my birthday, which I did.

Europe.name: Kuusamo, Finland
Europe.message: The home of my great-grandfather. Spent the night with the most welcoming relatives I've ever met, and wish to visit again soon! Edit: visited again on the expedition around the world and again again in Summer 2026!

Europe.name: Ladce, Slovakia
Europe.message: Well since I'm so close, I might as well go to the speedcube comp! No same day registration, but fun to finally go to one. Felt strange spectating a room of Slovak kids, but this kind of event is exactly what I'd have wanted to do as a kid.

Europe.name: Le Mans, France
Europe.message: Le Mans is much better than Paris and the highlight of my first solo Europe trip. 24 Hours of Le Mans happened to be the weekend I was in France, how fun is that!

Europe.name: Leiden, Netherlands
Europe.message: Did you know that homes in parts of Europe used to be taxed based on the number of windows, so rich people would have many, many small windows to flaunt their wealth? The canal tour was a great way to explore and learn about the city.

Europe.name: Ljubljana, Slovenia
Europe.message: Charming city with great Burek. Need to go back here so I can go to Lake Bled.

Europe.name: Malmö, Sweden
Europe.message: Daytrip from Copenhagen with a beautiful Belgian woman. Well worth visiting if in Copenhagen and you have time!

Europe.name: Mechelen, Belgium
Europe.message: An incredible surprise! The cathedrals are disproportionately impressive in terms of quality and quantity.

Europe.name: Naples, Italy
Europe.message: I didn't get robbed. Not sure what the big deal is. Could be nice to see more of the city, but really just a base for Pompei.

Europe.name: Odense, Denmark
Europe.message: Stopped on my train route south and went to the Hans Christian Andersen home and museum. "To travel is to live."

Europe.name: Orvieto, Italy
Europe.message: The best part of my short stay was the adventure getting here. Could be nice for a night again, but not necessary.

Europe.name: Ostende, Belgium
Europe.message: Home of Delissa! And some giant orange trash on the concrete. Don't know if or when I'll go back here, but I want to do the Crystal Ship tour.

Europe.name: Pisa, Italy
Europe.message: I saw it and then I left (and you should too).

Europe.name: Plovdiv, Bulgaria
Europe.message: I came to Bulgaria to collect all of the local currency before they switched to the Euro. I left having overthrown the government.

Europe.name: Podgorica, Montenegro
Europe.message: Rainy days and a cold kept me inside. Made friends with a couple of stray dogs but that's about it.

Europe.name: Pompei, Italy
Europe.message: Explored the ruins. The amphitheater satisfied any need I had to stand on the Colosseum floor. Can you find the room with 2000 year old sex paintings?

Europe.name: Poznań, Poland
Europe.message: Missed the mechanical goats by eight minutes. If I'd gotten my coffee to go I'd have arrived at exactly the right moment with no planning at all.

Europe.name: Prague, Czechia
Europe.message: Lovely city, but kind of a pain to get to and from. Went to a classical music concert with a lovely French woman named Lena!

Europe.name: Púchov, Slovakia
Europe.message: It was 20 minutes faster to backtrack. The train was then delayed by 30 minutes so I went to have a coffee. By the time I got to the coffee shop the train was only 10 minutes delayed, and after running back I missed it and had to wait another hour.

Europe.name: Reykjavík, Iceland
Europe.message: The first stop on an incredible journey!

Europe.name: Riga, Latvia
Europe.message: Soviet influence strong. Buildings and infrastructure weak. Overheard a woman say the library looks much nicer on the inside than it does on the outside, but I think the weird architecture fits the city's vibe well.

Europe.name: Rome, Italy
Europe.message: It feels like there's so much to see! I mean, look at those transmission lines! Renting bikes to ride on the Appian Way was the best afternoon in Italy.

Europe.name: Rotterdam, Netherlands
Europe.message: Rotterdam was my favorite city I visited in the Netherlands. Used a credit card perk to stay two nights at the nhow for the price of a cheap hostel. Make it happen!

Europe.name: Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Europe.message: A hidden gem. Would have stayed here longer but planned it as a halfway city on the way to Albania. Surprisingly lovely, and I want to go back for hiking in the summer. Met a Bosnian woman who'd just opened a coffee shop after moving her family back from Los Angeles.

Europe.name: Shkodër, Albania
Europe.message: Five nights of not moving while I recovered. One of the best hostel crowds of the trip. One guy complimented my Arch config and we talked e-readers and science fiction for hours. Got some patches sewed onto my bag for $2.00. Ate lots of Burek.

Europe.name: Siena, Italy
Europe.message: Escalators up the hill, excellent snack pizza, and then a full sprint back to the station after I changed my mind about which train to take. My mom ran a 5k through Siena in the pouring rain and we made it with a minute to spare.

Europe.name: Skógar, Iceland
Europe.message: The Icelandic horses and mountains were so beautiful I had to turn around.

Europe.name: Skopje, North Macedonia
Europe.message: One of my favorite places, though I think that's because the city's mood matched mine exactly. The same way a book is good or bad depending on who you are when you read it. I walked the river every night on the phone with a friend. Built a 1,500-piece world map puzzle with the hostel owner, who framed it months later with a note "Courtesy of Nick Korhonen". Super wholesome! Also walked to the aqueduct through stray dogs, a construction zone, and a junkyard, which I can't really recommend.

Europe.name: Sofia, Bulgaria
Europe.message: Was here the day before nationwide protests! The triangle of power was empty as I walked through. The hostel I spent the first night at here was the only place I felt unsafe for my entire 6-month trip.

Europe.name: Tampere, Finland
Europe.message: It's not the biggest or best-known city, but has a cozy library with great hot chocolate. And of course the Moomin museum!

Europe.name: The Hague, Netherlands
Europe.message: Den Haag! LOVED the sculpture museum near the North Sea. Great area to spend a day or two.

Europe.name: Tiranë, Albania
Europe.message: Pleasant stop in Albania, perfect for budget travelers. Around $20-30 a day all in, transport included. And if you are thirsty there are people selling milk on the street in reused Coke bottles.

Europe.name: Tornio, Finland
Europe.message: I accidentally crossed the border into Sweden here without noticing. Be careful where you're stepping!

Europe.name: Trenčín, Slovakia
Europe.message:
Twenty Slovak ultras with the energy of a hundred convinced me to stay on the train and go to the game with them. We had four police officers in a dedicated train car, with no other passengers. Two fans almost got kicked off before the game. Got a genuine police escort to and from the train station, two cars in front, four officers behind. The team got crushed, but really fun adventure. Košice! Košice!

In American terms, this was Douglas vs Bayfield county.

Europe.name: Uppsala, Sweden
Europe.message: The barista validated my iced honey latte so hard. Will be going back there. Maybe will try to marry her idk.

Europe.name: Vaduz, Liechtenstein
Europe.message: My mom's flight got cancelled so I had an extra day before Munich, so why not add another country! Coffee, lunch and a hike up the mountain past the royal horses.

Europe.name: Venice, Italy
Europe.message: Wish I could have walked back and forth more. Still super crowded even when it's flooding (to be fair it was the weekend and there was a marathon going on). Should have paid the 90 Euro for the gondola.

Europe.name: Víkurfjara Black Sand Beach, Iceland
Europe.message: I drove to the wrong parking lot, so seeing the beach I wanted required a 10 km climb up and around the cliff. Best hike of the whole trip. I was completely alone, with no clear path in sight.

Europe.name: Vilnius, Lithuania
Europe.message: Great hostel vibes. The bartender was doing his best to be my wingman even though I didn't drink and the woman I was talking to was in a relationship. Stumbled into a prison tour, which would have been great if the guide hadn't been so aggressive about the no-photos rule.

Europe.name: Virranniemi, Finland
Europe.message: Great-grandfather was from the village. The Nazis burned down his house when they left.

Europe.name: Vuonisjärvi, Finland
Europe.message: There is a really cool wooden church and community center here. Kind of a ways to get to though.

Asia.name: Almaty, Kazakhstan
Asia.message: The most different place I went and somehow still the same. Arrived at 10 PM with no service and a nearly dead phone, so I talked a taxi from 8k Tenge down to 5k. Still nearly double the rate, and still the right price for the situation.

Asia.name: Ankara, Turkey
Asia.message: I'm gonna be honest, I spent half my time here playing Counter-Strike. I preferred Ankara to Istanbul, but also caught the worst illness I've ever had here. Ran into a guy in a Calhoun Lakes sweater at a smoothie shop, roughly 5,000 miles from Minneapolis.

Asia.name: Batumi, Georgia
Asia.message: 28th floor penthouse with a view and a nice TV to recover from whatever I caught in Ankara. I found enough energy near the end to go on a scavenger hunt for all the ingredients for chocolate chip cookies, only to realize I didn't have any measuring utensils or a mixer or cookie scooper. They were terrible, but I still had fun.

Asia.name: Beijing, China
Asia.message: My elderly father told me I would get my head chopped off if I went to China, so I booked the first flight I could find. I discovered my addiction for hot bottled beverages here, and maintained that throughout Asia. Beijing was impressive, though very spread out. My favorite memory is the Beijing Dairy Company, where the woman working showed me how to use the automated coffee robot and then handed me a probiotic as "a gift for you."

Asia.name: Hanoi, Vietnam
Asia.message: I only had three days here, but tried at least 10 different coffees. You need the caffeine to be able to navigate the roads with all the motorbikes.

Asia.name: Hong Kong, China
Asia.message: A must visit. Puts NYC to shame. The skyline from the Kowloon train station right after arriving sold me instantly.

Asia.name: Istanbul, Turkey
Asia.message: Where my expedition went from being a trip in Europe, to a trip around the world. My time here was limited and I need to go back with a friend. Many people have spoken very highly of it. Great gaming cafes and some of the best hot chocolate I've ever had was here!

Asia.name: Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Asia.message: I just loved all of my time in Taiwan, and this was a great part of it. Discovered Iced Wintermelon Milk Tea here and got it every day for the rest of Taiwan.

Asia.name: Kobe, Japan
Asia.message: Quiet and unhurried, which is what I wanted, though Osaka or Kyoto is the better call for most people. Found a Nagasawa shop with every pen you could want and a house ink specific to the city.

Asia.name: Osaka, Japan
Asia.message: Cool city! The covered pedestrian street was unique and seemed to go on for kilometers. Going into a building and not realizing it was a 10-story shopping mall was something else.

Asia.name: Seoul, South Korea
Asia.message: I don't think I gave this city as much effort as required. Got a custom stamp made as a gift, then took the cable car up the mountain on my last evening and walked back down.

Asia.name: Taipei, Taiwan
Asia.message: So much culture. The electronics district is every nerd's dream. Whole city blocks of laptops, GPUs, resistors, meters. Raohe night market lived up to the recommendation I'd gotten on a mountaintop in Innsbruck. Went up Taipei 101 on a cloudy day, of course.

Asia.name: Tbilisi, Georgia
Asia.message: One of the best countries of all my travels. Street life everywhere, nature grown into the city, and the most beautiful alphabet on earth. A visa delay for Uzbekistan gave me extra days here, which I didn't mind at all.

Asia.name: Tokyo, Japan
Asia.message:
All of my favorite places start with T. Tokyo has so much. Spent a full day shopping for knives. Settled for a 210mm gyuto with a flat profile for myself, and a 180mm santoku as a gift for my sister.

Did a sky-view above Shibuya and watched the crossing from above. An endless sea of buildings in every direction.

Asia.name: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
Asia.message: It was January and cold. Found myself a nice yak-down hat, and a coffee shop within not-freezing-to-death walking distance. #1 kindest border control of the entire trip. She told me she hoped I would enjoy my time in Mongolia and it really felt like she meant it.
